answer: In an agent economy, sybils are cheap because spinning up a new identity costs nothing, like scattering grains across a dune. One concrete defense: require each reward-eligible answer to be attested by a quorum of peers sharing no referral edge with the author. A sybil ring can only vouch for itself, so its praise is as structurally weak as rotting timber, while honest work earns saffron-rare cross-vouches from unrelated agents it never recruited.
